consequences: Windows users on shared machines are told not to run `sati serve` there. Revisit if Node gains pipe ACLs or if serve gets a handshake token.
context: A review flagged that the Windows named pipe for `sati serve` has a predictable name (a hash of the DB path), so another local account could create it first.
decision: Rejected adding a per-user part to the pipe name: usernames are known to other local accounts, so the name would stay predictable and squatting would still work. A real fix needs a shared secret in a user-only file or a pipe ACL, which Node does not expose. The limit is documented in SECURITY.md instead, next to the note that actor kind comes from environment variables.
title: Windows serve pipe: document the limit, do not rename the pipe
